vocab.notes: ve before some consonant groups: ve městě, ve škole.
na poště, na nádraží, na náměstí
na poště (at the post office), na poštu (to the post office)
čekat na + accusative: Čekám na tebe. I'm waiting for you.

dialogue.setting: After work, Ondřej is waiting for his colleague Klára and calls her.

lines.speaker: Ondřej
lines.cs: Ahoj, kde jsi? Já už jsem na [[místě|místo|loc|location-v-na]].
lines.en: Hi, where are you? I'm already there.

spoken.form: Ahoj, kde seš? Já už sem na místě.
spoken.note: seš and sem for jsi and jsem.

lines.speaker: Klára
lines.cs: Promiň, jsem ještě v [[tramvaji|tramvaj|loc|location-v-na]]. Budu tam za deset [[minut|minuta|gen.pl|quantity-5plus]].
lines.en: Sorry, I'm still on the tram. I'll be there in ten minutes.

lines.speaker: Ondřej
lines.en: OK. I'm waiting in the café on the square.

lines.speaker: Klára
lines.en: In the café next to the museum?

lines.speaker: Klára
lines.en: Great, I'll be there in a moment.

exercises.prompt: Where is Klára, and when will she arrive?
exercises.listen: Promiň, jsem ještě v tramvaji. Budu tam za deset minut.
options: On the tram; in ten minutes
In the café; in two minutes
answers: On the tram; in ten minutes

hints.wrong: In the café; in two minutes
hints.explain: She's "v tramvaji", on the tram, and "za deset minut" is in ten minutes.
"V tramvaji" is on the tram; "za deset minut", in ten minutes.

exercises.why: "Promiň, jsem ještě v tramvaji. Budu tam za deset minut." Sorry, I'm still on the tram. I'll be there in ten minutes.

options: In the café on the square
answers: In the café on the square

hints.explain: The museum comes up next ("vedle muzea"). He's "v kavárně na náměstí".
A stop is "zastávka". He's waiting "v kavárně", in the café.

exercises.why: "Čekám v kavárně na náměstí." I'm waiting in the café on the square. v / na + locative.

lines: Promiň, jsem ještě v tramvaji. Budu tam za deset minut. Klára

hints.explain: "Za deset minut" is in ten minutes (deset = 10).
"Budu tam" means "I'll be there", in ten minutes.

exercises.why: "Sorry, I'm still on the tram. I'll be there in ten minutes. Klára"

answers: {Jsem ještě v tramvaji|Ještě jsem v tramvaji}[.]
exercises.why: See "Word order and the little words": new information goes last, and jsem, se, si, mi, ho… go second.
After v (in), use the locative. Before the ending -e, the h in Praha changes to z: v Praze.

hints.explain: After v (in), use the locative: Praha → v Praze.
Before -e the h in Praha changes to z: v Praze.
Prahu is the accusative (movement). For where you live, use the locative: v Praze.

exercises.why: v + location takes the locative. Feminine -a → -ě (or -e): kavárna → v kavárně.

hints.explain: After v (where?), use the locative: kavárna → v kavárně.
-u is the accusative, for movement. For location, use the locative: v kavárně.

exercises.question: Which case is "poště"?
exercises.why: na + location (where?) takes the locative: na poště. With movement (where to?) it's the accusative: Jdu na poštu.
"At home" is the fixed word doma.

hints.explain: v domě means "in the building/house". "At home" is simply doma.
domů means "(to) home", with movement. "At home" is doma.
kam is "where to" (movement). For location, use kde: Kde jsi?

exercises.prompt: I was waiting in the café. (a man says)
answers: {Čekal jsem v kavárně|V kavárně jsem čekal}[.]
exercises.why: See "Word order and the little words": new information goes last, and jsem, se, si, mi, ho… go second.

hints.explain: Jsem can't come first: it goes in the second position, after the first word. Čekal jsem v kavárně.
Jsem goes in the second position, straight after the first word: Čekal jsem v kavárně.

exercises.why: tramvaj is a soft feminine noun (like píseň): the locative ends in -i, v tramvaji.

hints.explain: tramvají (-í) is the instrumental: "by tram". In the tram is the locative: v tramvaji.
-ě is for hard nouns in -a (v kavárně). tramvaj is soft: v tramvaji.
That one is “Bydlím v Praze.”.
That one is “Já jsem doma.”.

exercises.why: Open spaces like squares and streets take na, not v: na náměstí, na ulici.
čekat is a class-5 verb: čekám, čekáš, čeká, čekáme, čekáte, čekají.

hints.explain: počkám is perfective, so it means "I'll wait". For "I'm waiting (now)", use the imperfective: čekám.

exercises.en: I'm waiting in the café on the square.
exercises.why: Happening now, in progress: the imperfective čekat → čekám.

hints.explain: Počkám is "I'll wait", a promise about what you'll do. Right now: čekám.

exercises.why: A promise about what you'll do next: the perfective počkat → počkám (its present form means the future).

hints.explain: Čekám is "I'm waiting" right now. Promising to wait: počkám.
